indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: B4.3.3.1 Describe the position of objects in space using the cardinal points
indicator.objective: Tell the position and motion of objects in space using the cardinal points north, south, east and west

skills.description: Identify North, South, East, and West on a compass or grid.
Describe where an object is relative to another using cardinal points.
Describe the movement of an object from one point to another using cardinal points.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4.
misconceptions: Thinking North is always up on any map, regardless of orientation.

questions.stem: If you are facing North, which direction is behind you?
hints: What is the opposite of North?
questions.misconception: Saying West because it's to the left.

questions.stem: On a map, if North is at the top, where is East?
questions.explanation: East is on the right side of a standard map.

questions.stem: Point X is at (1, 2) and Point Y is at (1, 1). What is the position of Y relative to X?
hints: Y has a smaller y-coordinate than X.
questions.explanation: Y is below X, so it is South.

questions.stem: To move from (2, 2) to (4, 2), in which direction do you travel?
questions.explanation: Moving right on a grid is East.

questions.stem: The hospital is North of the school. The market is East of the school. What is the position of the hospital relative to the market?
hints: Draw it: School at center. Hospital above. Market to the right.
From the market, the hospital is up and to the left.
questions.explanation: The hospital is North-West of the market.

questions.stem: Start at (3, 1). Move 2 squares South. What is the new y-coordinate?
Point A is at (5, 4) and Point B is at (2, 4). What is the position of A relative to B?
A pupil starts at (0, 0) and moves 4 squares East and 3 squares North. What is the new x-coordinate?
A point moves from (1, 5) to (1, 1). In which direction did it move?
If you face West, what is on your left?
questions.explanation: When facing West, South is to the left.

questions.stem: Start at (2, 3). Move 5 squares West. What is the new x-coordinate?
Explain how to move from (2, 2) to (5, 4) using cardinal directions.
questions.explanation: Move 3 squares East, then 2 squares North.
questions.misconception: Mixing up the order of movement.

questions.stem: Point C is at (0, 0) and Point D is at (0, -3). What is the position of D relative to C?
questions.misconception: Saying North because 3 is a large number.

questions.stem: A point is at (4, 4). It moves 3 squares North and 2 squares West. Where is it now?
questions.misconception: Swapping the changes to x and y.

questions.stem: A pupil starts at (1, 1). They move 2 East, then 3 North, then 2 West. What is their final position?
Start at (3, 2). Move 3 squares South, then 4 squares East. What is the new x-coordinate?
questions.misconception: Changing x by the South move too.

questions.stem: Point P is North of Q. Point R is East of Q. What is the direction of R from P?
hints: Draw Q at (0,0). P is (0,1). R is (1,0).
From P(0,1) to R(1,0), you go right and down.

questions.stem: A point starts at (2, 2) and moves to (-1, 5). What is the total change in the x-coordinate? (Enter as a negative number if decreasing)
A treasure map says: Start at (0,0). Go 3 km East, then 4 km North. What are the coordinates of the treasure?
